status_summary: Executive Order 14321 (2025-07-24) directed HUD and HHS to end support for Housing First policies and to raise treatment requirements, and HUD has pursued this through Continuum of Care funding notices rather than a change to 24 CFR part 578 or a statute. The Rhode Island district court's order of 2026-06-29 vacated HUD's November and December 2025 notices (per the court's later opinion), and HUD awarded about $3.85 billion in FY2025 renewals in 2026. HUD's FY2026 notice of 2026-06-01 offers about $4.04 billion, sets aside about $1.3 billion for new transitional-housing and services-only projects and adds scoring points for treatment and required supportive services, according to the Congressional Research Service. The district court set that notice aside on 2026-08-07 for lack of notice and comment, the First Circuit stayed that ruling on 2026-09-16 and, on plaintiffs' motion, entered judgment on 2026-09-24 vacating it and remanding the remaining claims (per the district court docket), and HUD reopened the notice on 2026-09-18 with applications due 2026-09-30; HUD's program page listed no FY2026 awards as of 2026-10-22.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14321 signed; Section 5 directs HUD and HHS to end support for Housing First policies and HUD to increase treatment requirements for participants with substance use disorder or serious mental illness.

A state coalition sues over HUD's FY2025 Continuum of Care notice (issued in November 2025, which de-emphasized Housing First); a separate suit by cities and nonprofits follows on 2025-12-01. A court enters a preliminary injunction in December 2025 and HUD withdraws and later reopens the prior-year notice.

HUD announces the first round of FY2025 Continuum of Care renewal awards ($349 million for 622 projects); later rounds follow on 2026-04-27 and 2026-05-21, totaling about $3.85 billion, under the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75).
HUD abandons its appeal of the December 2025 preliminary injunction (month only known; reported by the California Attorney General, so dated to the first of the month).

HUD issues the FY2026 Continuum of Care NOFO: about $4.04 billion total, about $1.3 billion (roughly 30 percent) set aside for new transitional-housing and services-only projects, 60 percent of annual renewal demand available in tier 1 (the statutory minimum), and scoring points for treatment and recovery services and for requiring participation in supportive services (CRS). A lawsuit follows on 2026-07-02 and HUD modifies the notice on 2026-07-24.

D.R.I. Judge Mary McElroy rules HUD's 2025 overhaul of the program violated the Administrative Procedure Act and vacates HUD's November and December 2025 NOFOs (per the court's 2026-08-07 background); she declines to bar similar future changes or to fold the FY2026 notice into the same case (Maryland Matters).

Judge McElroy (State of Washington v. HUD, 1:26-cv-00439; NAEH v. HUD, 1:26-cv-00436) grants summary judgment in part and sets aside the FY2026 NOFO in its entirety: the roughly $1.3 billion set-aside requires notice and comment under 42 U.S.C. 11386b(d)(2)(C), which HUD did not provide; the court denies a permanent injunction against future versions, does not reach the other challenges (including OMB apportionment footnotes) and does not rule on whether the policy shift from Housing First is lawful on its merits. HUD appeals on 2026-08-13.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island (via govinfo)

timeline.event: A First Circuit panel (Nos. 26-1922 and 26-1923, consolidated) grants HUD a stay pending appeal of the district court's vacatur, per HUD and CRS; HUD reopens the FY2026 NOFO on 2026-09-18 with a 2026-09-30 deadline.

Plaintiffs (National Alliance to End Homelessness) report their emergency First Circuit motion, dated 2026-09-21, asking the court to vacate the district court ruling and remand so other claims can be heard, or alternatively to expedite the appeal (see 2026-09-24). The First Circuit stay order found HUD likely to succeed on the argument that the $1.3 billion set-aside is not a bonus or incentive covered by the comment requirement, and HUD has until 2026-12-01 to award the funds.
timeline.source: National Alliance to End Homelessness / JURIST

timeline.event: The First Circuit (Judges Montecalvo, Aframe and Dunlap; Nos. 26-1922 and 26-1923) enters judgment, docketed as vacated and remanded, on HUD's appeal of the district court's 2026-08-07 set-aside of the FY2026 notice, after plaintiffs moved on 2026-09-21 for summary vacatur of the notice-and-comment ruling and remand of their other claims; the mandate issues 2026-09-28, and at a 2026-09-29 status conference the district court sets supplemental briefs for 2026-09-30, responses for 2026-10-07 and replies for 2026-10-14 (per the district court docket as mirrored by the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse; the judgment text was not read).

title: End Housing First requirements and shift homelessness funding toward treatment first
uncertainties: Sources conflict on what HUD did in December 2025: the California Attorney General and a law-firm summary say a preliminary injunction required HUD to keep the prior-year NOFO and HUD reopened it in January 2026, while Smart Cities Dive describes a December reissue with similar policy changes and Maryland Matters reports a new NOFO on 2025-12-19; the Rhode Island court's 2026-08-07 opinion says its 2026-06-29 order vacated both the November and December 2025 notices, but the 2025 and June 2026 orders themselves were not read. The San Francisco City Attorney (2026-04-01) and Scotsman Guide report that the First Circuit declined on 2026-04-01 to set aside the preliminary order on the FY2025 notice, which differs from the California Attorney General's description of HUD abandoning its appeal. The August 2026 opinion and the CRS Insight were read through fetch summaries; the First Circuit stay order was not read (the Leagle page shows only an introduction), so its reasoning rests on JURIST and a case-tracker docket summary; the 2026-12-01 award deadline is also stated in the plaintiffs' motion. The exact date of the November 2025 NOFO is as reported by news outlets. HUD's page says the district court ruled to vacate the FY2026 notice and the court's order says it set the notice aside. The plaintiffs' emergency motion asking the First Circuit to vacate and remand or to expedite is dated 2026-09-21 on the filing, while the National Alliance to End Homelessness post describing it is dated 2026-09-22. The 2026-09-24 First Circuit judgment is known from its district court docket entry, which reads only vacated and remanded, as mirrored by the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse; the judgment and any accompanying opinion were not read, and the reading that it vacates the 2026-08-07 set-aside and returns the other notice claims to the district court rests on the plaintiffs' 2026-09-21 motion, which asked for that relief and offered to drop the notice-and-comment claim because HUD began a comment process on 2026-09-11 (91 FR 57901). The district court's 2026-10-16 notice and the supplemental briefs were not read, and no district court ruling on the remaining claims was found as of 2026-10-22. A separate HUD Federal Register notice on incentivized homelessness-reduction activities (comments due 2026-10-13) was not read. No rule change to 24 CFR part 578 and no statute was located. As context only, the House Appropriations Committee reported the FY2027 THUD bill (H.R. 9170) on 2026-06-05 with about $4.16 billion for Homeless Assistance Grants, against $4.42 billion enacted for FY2026 and a $4.02 billion request (CRS); CRS describes no Housing First or treatment conditions, the bill's homeless assistance paragraph was not read, and the bill has not passed the House.
